newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Svyazinvest group may bring in Western telecoms co.
newsitem.headline: Svyazinvest group may bring in Western telecoms co.

text.p: The financial consortium which won a tender last week for one quarter of Russian telecoms holding company Svyazinvest will hold the stake for at least two years, and may bring in a major Western telecoms operator, the leader of the consortium, Uneximbank, said on Thursday.

Uneximbank President Vladimir Potanin told a news conference that the consortium was working on a programme to issue "derivatives" on the Svyazinvest shares in Western markets in the next six to nine months, and said Uneximbank was considering bidding in a second tender for a 24 percent stake in Svyazinvest, open to Russian investors only.

The victory of the Uneximbank consortium, comprising Russian and foreign financial institutions, has sparked a huge row in Russia in which one criticism levelled at the victors is that they do not include a telecoms operator. The losing consortium in Russia's biggest privatisation to date included Spain's Telefonica.

"Our plans include bringing in an operator," he said. There are no other major telecoms operators in Russia, meaning the consortium would have to look abroad. Asked whether Telefonica was a possibility, Potanin said he could not rule that out.

"We are considering the possibility of taking part in the second tender, since the investment in Svyazinvest for us is a strategic one, so the next sale is of great interest," said Potanin, who was briefly first deputy prime minister until March.

The agreement among the consortium members, who include Deutsche Bank's Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Morgan Stanley Asset Management, and U.S. financier George Soros, foresees holding on to the shares for two years, but Uneximbank intended to hold on to its shares for longer than that, he said. He said it was too early to give details on the planned issue of derivative securities on the Svyazinvest shares.
